label: ILLUSTRATIVE animation with source-informed timing; not motion capture, not simulated behaviour; no predator AI, contact physics, retinal stimulus or neural response

conventions.playback: clip seconds are estimated physical seconds; playback multiplier default 1
conventions.inplace_vs_rootmotion:
*_inplace keeps

_motion fixed (feet slide back in stance); *_rootmotion moves it so stance feet stay planted
conventions.turns: turn_left = heading rotates toward +X, the anatomical left in a right-handed +Y-up, +Z-forward frame; side letters are anatomical (L at +X) since v3; mount without reflection (see ENV_HANDEDNESS_PROOF.json)
conventions.scale: predators use their own viewport-mm-per-mm factor (parameters), not the fly 3.3x

checks.glb: rest reset vs rig GLB; DOF limits over the whole duration at 240 Hz incl. loop seam; key and seam continuity < 0.5 rad; FK ground check of every leg vertex; stance-foot slide per 240 Hz sample <= 0.01 viewport-mm in root-motion clips (stance intervals from metadata); travel heading +Z and speed within 5 % for walk_forward_rootmotion
checks.blender: every frame: leg-into-body penetration (ray parity, hip sockets excluded), IK target error, lowest leg vertex vs foot plane, display limits
checks.not_checked: leg-to-leg contact; the composed walk-scene GLB is the clips GLB plus a ground node and is hashed but not re-verified separately; 2D sprites are checked only by their documented camera/scale, not by image analysis

environment.node: wind_vane_rotor (child of env_wind_vane); rotate about +Y only

telemetry.frame: arena (x, y), as published by the dashboard telemetry (see the W1 sensory contract)

environment.frame_map: arena (x, y) -> three.js (x - cx, ., -(y - cy)) (INTERFACE.md arenaPointFor3D); a wind vector (wx, wy) is therefore (wx, 0, -wy) in the viewport
environment.formula: rotor yaw theta = atan2(wx, -wy) radians about +Y; the rotor local +Z (arrow tip) then points where the air moves TO (downwind); the orange fin trails upwind

checks.(wx, wy) = (0, +1): theta = atan2(0, -1) = pi: arrow points to viewport -Z, i.e. arena +y
checks.(wx, wy) = (+1, 0): theta = pi/2: arrow points to viewport +X, i.e. arena +x

environment.zero_or_missing: speed below 1e-6 mm/s, non-finite values or no wind field: leave the rotor at rest and show NOT SIMULATED; never animate
environment.magnitude: the vane shows direction only; show the speed as a number with units, not as vane motion

env_jumping_spider_rig.gait_label: source-informed (salticid tetrapod phase; tarantula duty proxy; stride timing low confidence)

parameters.stance_clearance_class: A: feet set 0.005 viewport-mm above the bind-pose foot plane so the slight idle body pitch never dips a claw below it
parameters.body_length_class: M (5.5-7.5 female, 4.0-7.0 male; araneae.nmbe.ch; Parigi et al. 2019)
parameters.speed_class: D/M: 15 mm/s is the lower end of the derived speed-while-moving range (15-25 mm/s; Shamble et al. 2017 Table S1 and stationary fraction) and equals the high-speed-video-based design speed (Shamble 2017 section 2e); overall mean including stops is 8.6 mm/s

gait.cycle_class: D, L confidence: 8 full steps in 1.2 s (De Agro et al. 2021 Methods) gives 0.15-0.3 s strides (3-7 Hz); 0.2 s (5 Hz, mid-range) chosen so the 15 mm/s stride stays within the rig's leg reach
gait.duty_class: P, L-M confidence: tarantula Grammostola rosea 0.63-0.70 (Hao et al. 2019 Table 2)
gait.phase_class: M (qualitative): alternating tetrapod, set A = R1 L2 R3 L4 and set B = L1 R2 L3 R4 (letters on the anatomical side since v3; same two antiphase sets) in antiphase; forelegs walk (Shamble 2017 Fig. 1 caption, Fig. 2d, non-mimetic salticid controls)

turn.yaw_rate_class: D: one of eight legs steps every ~9 deg of turn (Land 1972 abstract) at the 0.2 s stride -> 360 deg/s, inside the measured 120-1200 deg/s
turn.note: turn-side legs move backward and the other side forward relative to the body, as Land 1972 describes; step amplitude here is set by the rig limits, not the 75 deg reported

start_stop.class: A (stops 0.1-1.5 s as in the Shamble 2017 playback design; fast acceleration assumed)

idle.class: A: legs still and forelegs down when stationary (Shamble 2017, M qualitative); palp flicks and slight body pitch are artistic

labels.gait: source-informed (salticid tetrapod phase; tarantula duty proxy; stride timing low confidence)

scene_walk.class: A: composed sequence (stop-and-go as Shamble 2017 describes); timing of each part artistic

views: top, fixed camera over the ground

_scale.note: mesh extent includes palps/mouthparts (spider) or head-to-abdomen-tip (mantis)

env_mantis_nymph_rig.gait_label: cross-species proxy / artistic estimate (no mantis walking kinematics published)

parameters.stance_clearance_class: A: feet set 0.02 viewport-mm above the bind-pose foot plane so the flexed tibia end never dips below it
parameters.body_length_class: M (10-15 mm first instar; Parigi et al. 2019 Methods)
parameters.speed_class: A, L confidence: no mantis walking kinematics found; 3-15 mm/s (0.3-1.0 BL/s) stop-and-go estimate

gait.cycle_class: P/D, L confidence: 0.34-0.85 s adult stick insect (Grabowska et al. 2012); nymph scaling not established, same period used at 1x
gait.duty_class: D, L confidence: 0.7-0.8 from the walk/wave gait definition (Grabowska 2012 Fig. 2)
gait.phase_class: P: four-leg walk with a back-to-front wave, phi(R2->R3) 0.73, phi(R2->L3) 0.22, phi(R2->L2) 0.52 from adult Carausius morosus with front legs amputated (Grabowska 2012 Figs 6-8); offsets = -phi; v3 letters on the anatomical side: the same curves on the same physical legs, so the offsets read L2 0, L3 0.27, R3 0.78, R2 0.48 (mirror image of the proxy, equally valid by symmetry)

parameters.raptorial_forelegs: held folded and raised, not used for walking (A with secondary support: Grabowska 2012 Introduction)

turn.mode: orienting turn on the spot with a ballistic head/body onset
turn.yaw_rate_class: A: turn duration not available (0.2-0.5 s per orienting turn suggested); 45 deg over 2 gait cycles here so the legs can step
turn.head_lead_class: M (abstract): head, prothorax and abdomen rotations start within 40 ms (Yamawaki et al. 2011, T. aridifolia, life stage not stated)

idle.class: D under a labelled scaling assumption: peering sway 2-3 mm at 2-2.5 mm/s (adult Kral 2012 values x 12.5/70); body translates sideways while the head keeps facing forward

labels.gait: cross-species proxy / artistic estimate (no mantis walking kinematics published)

scene_walk.class: A: composed stop-and-go sequence (Kral 2012 qualitative); timing artistic

views: top, fixed camera over the ground
